subsystems.name: Direct air capture unit
subsystems.role: extracts carbon dioxide from ambient air to feed the microbes.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: provides a controlled, sterile environment where microbes consume gases and multiply.
parts: sensors for pH, temperature, and dissolved gases

subsystems.name: Engineered microbial strain
subsystems.role: converts CO2, nitrogen, and hydrogen into edible protein through synthetic metabolic pathways.
parts: synthetic genes for carbon fixation and nitrogen assimilation

subsystems.name: Gas and nutrient supply
subsystems.role: delivers hydrogen as an energy source and nitrogen as a building block.

subsystems.name: Harvesting and processing
subsystems.role: separates microbial cells from the broth and turns them into food-grade protein.
parts: cell disruption and nucleic acid removal

buildSteps.title: Engineer the microbe
buildSteps.detail: Use synthetic biology to insert or optimise metabolic pathways so the strain can grow on carbon dioxide, hydrogen, and nitrogen, while producing high levels of protein.

buildSteps.title: Set up gas supply
buildSteps.detail: Install a water electrolyser powered by renewable electricity to make hydrogen, and a unit to separate nitrogen from air.

buildSteps.title: Capture CO2 from air
buildSteps.detail: Build a direct air capture plant that uses a sorbent to pull carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and releases it in concentrated form.

buildSteps.title: Build the bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate a sealed vessel with efficient gas mixing, sterilisation, and sensors for pH, temperature, and pressure.

buildSteps.title: Inoculate and grow
buildSteps.detail: Start with a small culture of the engineered microbe, feed it hydrogen, CO2, nitrogen, and minerals, and let it multiply under controlled conditions.

buildSteps.title: Harvest biomass
buildSteps.detail: Continuously remove broth, separate the cells with a centrifuge or filter, and dry them into a protein-rich powder.

buildSteps.title: Process into food-grade protein
buildSteps.detail: Break open the cells, remove nucleic acids and cell walls, and purify the protein to meet food safety standards.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Move from lab-scale to pilot and then commercial plants, combining direct air capture, electrolysis, and bioreactors into a single continuous process.

prerequisites.why: DAC is demonstrated in small plants but remains energy-intensive and expensive, so it must become cheaper and more efficient to supply CO2 at scale.
Pilot plants already produce protein from industrial CO2 and hydrogen, but integration with atmospheric CO2 is not yet demonstrated.
Microbes can be engineered, but optimising them for high yield, genetic stability, and food safety takes years of research.
Renewable power is available, but making hydrogen and running DAC cheaply enough for competitive protein requires further cost reductions.
Edible proteins from engineered microbes must pass extensive safety testing and receive approval before they can be sold.

pathway.milestone: Pilot plants use captured industrial CO2 and hydrogen to produce edible protein.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that gas fermentation can yield safe, nutritious protein at small scale.

pathway.milestone: Integrate direct air capture with bioreactors so the process runs on atmospheric CO2.
pathway.unlocks: Independence from industrial CO2 sources, allowing production anywhere with renewable power.

pathway.milestone: Scale up to commercial plants and cut costs through learning and larger equipment.
pathway.unlocks: Protein that can compete on price with conventional agriculture.

pathway.milestone: Widespread deployment of atmospheric protein synthesis as a land-efficient food source.
pathway.unlocks: Reduced pressure on land, water, and fertiliser, and more resilient food supply.
